$comment: Metric-action rule registry. See shared/mesh_runtime/metric_action_rules.py for the full format spec. Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins. Put more specific rules before more general ones. Every rule carries its own bounds — the engine enforces those at match time, so a typo cannot produce a runaway actuation.

rules.name: scale on node pressure
rules.$doc: Node memory or disk pressure can starve pods even when the deployment is otherwise healthy. Scaling the affected deployment within bounded replica limits gives the scheduler room to place new pods while preserving human review for storage-specific pressure rules.
rules.rollback_plan: scale deployment back to the prior replica count if node pressure does not clear within 10 minutes

rules.name: scale on consumer lag
rules.$doc: Covers Kafka consumer lag, RabbitMQ queue depth, Celery backlog, and SQS approximate-messages metrics. A single rule fires across the four queue technologies because they all look like 'unread messages climbing'. Only triggers at ≥30% delta so transient bursts don't churn replicas.
rules.rollback_plan: scale deployment back to the prior replica count if the lag does not drop within 10 minutes

rules.name: scale on cpu saturation
rules.$doc: CPU utilization crossing 85% typically responds well to adding replicas, especially for stateless workloads. Note we match on the OTel semantic convention metric names (system.cpu.utilization, process.cpu.utilization) plus the common Prometheus-style node_cpu_seconds_total variants.
rules.rollback_plan: scale back down once CPU utilization returns below 60% for 10 minutes

rules.name: restart on memory saturation
rules.$doc: When memory.usage climbs toward memory.limit, the workload is usually close to OOMKill. A rolling restart clears the pressure and buys time while the operator reviews for a real leak. (A future patch_resources rule would raise the limit instead, but the actuator isn't wired yet.)
rules.rollback_plan: if memory pressure returns within 10 minutes, escalate for a real leak investigation

rules.name: scale on request rate spike
rules.$doc: Broad fallback for latency-adjacent metrics: request rate, concurrent connections, active sessions. Fires only at 50% delta to keep it conservative — request rate moves a lot naturally. Consumer-lag and CPU rules above will usually fire first for known workloads.
rules.rollback_plan: scale back to prior replica count once the traffic burst subsides

rules.name: restart on solana slot lag
rules.$doc: Fires when a Solana validator falls >128 slots (~50s) behind the reference cluster head. Slot lag this large usually means the process has stalled on disk I/O, GC, or a gossip partition; a rolling restart clears transient state. NOT an appropriate response if the validator is actively voting — operators should review `vote_in_progress` in related_context before approving. Risk level is medium so the approval gate fires by default.
rules.rollback_plan: no rollback — the restart is the remediation; escalate if lag persists >5m after restart

rules.name: restart on geth peer starvation
rules.$doc: Fires when a geth/reth node is below the configured minimum peer count. Zero or very-low peers usually means the discovery service is stuck or the network interface has a routing issue; a restart re-seeds peer discovery. Also fires on reth via the shared `mesh.node.kind` attribute.
rules.rollback_plan: no rollback — if peers do not recover within 5 minutes, escalate to network team
